name: Anifrolumab
drug_class: Anti-type I interferon receptor monoclonal antibody

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ antibody against subunit 1 of the type I interferon receptor. Year of first patent filing (priority June 2004, Medarex, US 7,662,381).

tagline: Type I interferon receptor blocker for moderate to severe lupus
summary: Anifrolumab is a human monoclonal antibody that blocks the type I interferon receptor. It targets the 'interferon signature' prominent in systemic lupus erythematosus and was approved in 2021 for moderate to severe SLE in patients on standard therapy.
mechanism: Most patients with SLE show increased expression of type I interferon-inducible genes. Type I interferons (IFN-α, IFN-β, IFN-ω and others) signal through the IFNAR1/IFNAR2 receptor and JAK1/TYK2.
Anifrolumab binds IFNAR1, blocking signalling by all type I interferons and causing the receptor to be internalised. This reduces interferon-driven activation of dendritic cells, B cells and T cells.
uses: Moderate to severe systemic lupus erythematosus in adults receiving standard therapy

history.title: MUSE
history.detail: Phase 2 MUSE trial shows benefit in SLE, especially with a high interferon signature.

history.title: TULIP-1
history.detail: The first phase 3 trial misses its primary endpoint.

history.title: TULIP-2
history.detail: The second phase 3 trial meets its primary endpoint (BICLA response).

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Approved in the European Union in February.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: TULIP-1 missed its SRI-4 primary endpoint, whereas TULIP-2 met its BICLA primary endpoint; approval rested on the combined evidence.
Herpes zoster is notably more frequent than with placebo.
